name: Underwriter
statusNote: Slice 1 of 5 shipped and running (connection, probes, recorder, calendar, diagnostics); the scanner, scores, gamma map, and exit engine are designed in the SPEC but not fully built.
oneLiner: A read-only decision-support desk for selling 0DTE SPX/SPXW credit spreads — it continuously answers whether selling today's options is a defensible idea, and never places an order.

dataFlow: TWS/IB Gateway (Read-Only API on) feeds a background engine thread.
It subscribes the SPX index, the ES front-quarterly, and the options chain via secdef discovery.
The engine cycle runs the math crates: expected move via straddle interpolation, realized vol, gamma map, spread scoring, breaker math.
The recorder writes 14 IPC streams plus a continuous journal — the single source of truth; breaker state is recomputed from it at every launch.
The UI polls Tauri IPC snapshots into the scanner, gamma map, expected-move, and position panels.
Any critical state fans out to a Discord webhook, a cockpit sound, and a Windows toast simultaneously.
integrations: Interactive Brokers TWS (Read-Only API, its own client id)
CBOE delayed JSON for open interest
decisions: The read-only law is enforced three ways: no order module is ever compiled in, TWS Read-Only API is checked, and no IPC command can describe an order.
Show nothing rather than something false — unverifiable values are named states (EM_UNAVAILABLE, TWS DOWN), never fabricated.
Breaker state is recomputed from the journal at every launch, never persisted — a restart-to-bypass exploit is structurally impossible.
Accept-and-flag: it never refuses to monitor a position; violations are flagged and journaled, not hidden.
All expected-move math derives from the interpolated ATM straddle mid; broker IV never enters a time-scaling formula.
KPI honesty — the UI states unconditional 0DTE selling is roughly zero-EV after frictions; POP is never presented as edge.
